intended_object: For a trace-zero matrix X ∈ sl_n(R), the element I + εX of SL_n(R[ε][η]). Here R[ε] is the inner dual-number ring, and the element is viewed as constant in the outer dual variable η. It is the "epsilon" factor in the mixed commutator (I+εX)(I+ηY)(I+εX)⁻¹(I+ηY)⁻¹ = I + εη[X,Y]. I inferred this from the docstring, the module documentation and the lemmas `epsilonLiftSL_val`, `epsilonLiftSL_reduce` and `epsilon_eta_SL_commutator`.
explanation:
`liftMatrix X` is the matrix whose (i,j) entry is (δ_ij, X_ij) in DualNumber R, so it is I + εX. `liftSL X` packages this as an element of SL_n(R[ε]): its determinant is 1 + ε·tr X, which equals 1 because tr X = 0. `epsilonLiftSL` then pushes this element into SL_n(R[ε][η]) along the inclusion of constants R[ε] → R[ε][η], using `Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.map` with `algebraMap`. That is exactly the "outer-constant embedding of the inner infinitesimal" that the docstring describes. The library's lemmas agree: its outer reduction gives back `liftSL X`, its image in GL matches the GL version, and the commutator identity with the eta factor gives the εη-multiple of the Lie bracket.

The generality is natural: R is any commutative ring and n is any finite index type with decidable equality, which the definition of SL_n needs. Mathlib has no ready-made element "I + εX in SL_n over dual numbers" that this definition duplicates. It is a specific auxiliary element for the commutator computation, but it is a well-defined mathematical object and it is formalized correctly.
